v1e.firmware: Requires FluidNC on V1 Engineering's Jackpot board: the program start, tool change and end use FluidNC commands. GRBL, grblHAL and Marlin builds aren't supported yet.
v1e.manualRouter: Manual router (e.g. a Makita RT0701C): set its speed on its dial; the G-code sets none.
v1e.jackpotGcode: The program start, tool change and end are V1 Engineering's Jackpot G-code. The start zeroes X, Y and Z where the bit is and probes Z with a 0.5 mm touch plate, so jog to the project's zero point first and use the stock top as Z zero. M62 P1 and M63 P1 switch an optional router relay on pin 27.

longmill.firmware: Requires Sienci's LongBoard (GRBL 1.1h, LongMill MK2) or SuperLongBoard (grblHAL, LongMill MK2.5).
longmill.spindle: Spindle: no router ships with the LongMill. Tick Manual spindle for a router set by its dial (e.g. a Makita RT0701), or enter the speed range of a controlled spindle, e.g. 7,500–24,000 RPM for Sienci's 1.5 kW spindle kit.
longmill.workArea: The work area is the smaller of the firmware's maximum travel ($130–$132) and Sienci's advertised area.
longmill.maxFeedZ: Max feed Z is the LongBoard's 3000 mm/min; the SuperLongBoard allows 4000 mm/min.
longmill.homing: Homing is off by default: zero X, Y and Z on the stock, e.g. with a touch plate.
longmill.advertised12x30: Sienci advertises 820 × 368 mm, with about 125 mm of Z; the firmware's 810 × 355 × 120 mm is used.
longmill.advertised30x30: Sienci advertises 820 × 868 mm, with about 125 mm of Z; the firmware's 810 × 855 × 120 mm is used.
longmill.advertised48x30: Sienci advertises 48 × 30 in (1219.2 × 762 mm), which this preset uses for X and Y; the firmware allows 1270 × 855 mm.

genmitsu.firmware: Runs GRBL 1.1h on its included controller, which ships configured for the machine.
genmitsu.maxFeedZ: Max feed Z: SainSmart gives one maximum speed, not one per axis. Send $$ in your G-code sender and enter $112, the Z axis maximum rate in mm/min.
genmitsu.spindle: Spindle: the stock 775 spindle is rated 9,000 RPM, and SainSmart publishes no minimum. Enter the slowest and fastest speeds you run it at, in RPM. The G-code's S words are in RPM, so GRBL's $30 (maximum spindle speed) should match the maximum.
genmitsu.rexSwitches: Has X, Y and Z limit switches for homing, and a Z probe for setting Z zero.
genmitsu.proverWorkArea: The work area is the user manual's; the product page lists 290 mm of X.
genmitsu.proverSwitches: Has home and limit switches, and a Z probe for setting Z zero.

lowrider.workArea: Work area: the usable cutting area you built for, as entered in V1 Engineering's LowRider calculator (X is the beam, the shorter axis), e.g. 1220 × 2440 mm for a full sheet. To check a finished build, jog the bit between opposite corners of the area it can reach and note the distance on each axis.
lowrider.zTravel: Z travel is the 50 mm cutting depth of a standard build; with a drop table you can use up to 100 mm.
lowrider.endstops: The endstops only act while homing and soft limits are off: keep the job inside your work area.

mpcnc.workArea: Work area: the X and Y build area you chose in V1 Engineering's MPCNC calculator, the area the tool can reach (e.g. 450 × 330 mm with the kit's belt). Larger tools such as a DeWalt DW660 or a spindle reach less of it. To check a finished build, jog the bit between opposite corners of the area it can reach and note the distance on each axis.
mpcnc.zTravel: Z travel: the Z build size from the calculator; 81 mm is the shortest, and the one V1 Engineering recommends.
mpcnc.limits: Z isn't homed, and soft limits are off: keep the job inside your work area.

maslow.firmware: Runs Maslow's own build of FluidNC, which comes on the Maslow 4 board.
maslow.area: Keep the job inside the area you can cut. The firmware has no limit switches: it flattens moves outside its work area (2440 × 1220 mm by default, centred on the frame) onto its edge instead of stopping. Trace Boundary shows the outline before cutting.
maslow.router: Switch the router (a DeWalt DWP611, or D26200 for 240 V) on and set its speed by hand; the G-code sets none.
maslow.maxFeeds: Max feeds are the lower official figures: the firmware's 2000 mm/min belt rate (the spec says 2500 mm/min X/Y) and the spec's 300 mm/min Z (the firmware allows 400).
maslow.zTravel: Z travel is the spec's 50 mm; the work area is listed as 65 mm deep.
maslow.zZero: Set Z zero on the stock top with Define Z Home.

Operation.roughingLinearHint: Straight zig-zag passes at an angle, rising over the model where it is higher

boundaryHints.model: The tool's centre reaches the edges of the model's outline.
boundaryHints.margin: Clears a frame this wide around the model's outline (at least the tool's radius), keeping the tool inside it: the stock top beyond is left for zeroing Z after a tool change.
boundaryHints.stock: The tool's centre reaches the edges of the stock: everything around the model is cleared down to its bottom.

finishBoundaryHints.model: The tool's centre reaches the edges of the model's outline.
finishBoundaryHints.margin: Also finishes a frame this wide around the model's outline (at least the tool's radius) down to the model's bottom, or the parting plane on a two-sided project, keeping the tool inside it, like roughing with the same margin.
finishBoundaryHints.stock: The tool's centre reaches the edges of the stock: everything around the model is finished down to its bottom, or the parting plane on a two-sided project.

Operation.finishBoundaryWaterline: Waterline contours follow the model's walls and stay on its outline: the margin and the whole stock only apply to parallel and spiral passes.

finishingHints.parallel: Straight passes at an angle. Best on gentle slopes; steep faces along the passes come out rough.
finishingHints.waterline: Contours at constant height, a step-down apart, so steep faces get as many passes as flat ones get few. Flat areas between contours aren't cut.
finishingHints.spiral: One continuous cut spiralling over the model's outline, with no retracts.

Operation.name: Name
Operation.catalog: Catalog (starting feeds for softwood and plywood)
Operation.selectToCut: Select shapes or paths to cut them instead
Operation.needsShape: An operation needs at least one shape
Operation.rampStraight: The tool's plunge angle is 90°, so it plunges straight down.
Operation.linearDirection: Linear passes alternate direction; this one applies to the laps and the finish pass.
Operation.finishLap: One lap on the walls and islands at full depth.
Operation.drillHint: Holes at the points and circles. The tool plunges into the points and the circles it fits within {tolerance}{bore, select, yes {, and bores larger circles with a helix at its plunge angle.} other {; a drill bit can't bore larger circles.}}
Operation.peckHint: Plunges in pecks no deeper than the tool's step-down, retracting after each to clear chips.
Operation.engraveHint: {side, select, inside {Follows the closed paths inside the line, with an edge of the groove on it,} outside {Follows the closed paths outside the line, with an edge of the groove on it,} other {Follows every path, open and closed, on the line,}} in passes no deeper than the tool's step-down.
Operation.lineTooDeep: Deeper than the cone, so the line is as wide as the bit.
Operation.lineAtTop: At the stock top, from the bit's {angle}° angle.
Operation.lineAtTopTip: At the stock top, from the bit's {angle}° angle and {tip} tip.
Operation.vcarveHint: Follows the middle of the closed paths, as deep as the bit's angle needs to reach their edges, in passes no deeper than the tool's step-down. Islands stay standing.
Operation.vcarveTooDeep: Deeper than the cone, so the bit carves no deeper than {depth}.
Operation.flatOn: The end mill clears those parts flat first; the V-bit then carves their walls.
Operation.flatOffer: Clear the parts that reach the max depth flat with an end mill.
Operation.flatNeedTool: Add a flat end mill to your tool library to clear a flat bottom.
Operation.roughHint: Clears the material above the model in levels, from the top only, leaving the stock to leave for finishing.
Operation.roughStrategyHint: {hint}, in levels no more than the tool's step-down ({stepDown}) apart.
Operation.restHint: Skips what the enabled operations above this one already cut, so a smaller tool only works where the last one couldn't reach.
Operation.finishHint: Passes over the model, the tool dropped onto it at every point, from the top only. A ball end mill leaves the smoothest surface.
Operation.spacingHint: Of the tool's diameter: {spiral, select, yes {laps} other {passes}} {spacing} apart at most.
Operation.zigzagHint: Every other pass comes back, linked along the model.
Operation.oneWayHint: Every pass cuts the same way, retracting in between.
Operation.placeTitle: Replace the tabs with ones spread evenly along each contour
Operation.editHint: Click a contour to add a tab, drag a tab to move it, click it to remove it.
Operation.pinDepth: As deep as the pin settings say: {depth}.

Selection.shapes: {count, plural, one {# selected shape} other {# selected shapes}}
Selection.paths: {count, plural, one {# selected path} other {# selected paths}}
Selection.both: {shapes, plural, one {# selected shape} other {# selected shapes}} and {paths, plural, one {# path} other {# paths}}

Operations.sideways: Add an end mill or a V-bit to your tool library: drill bits can't cut sideways

hints.drill: Drill the points and circles of the {target}
hints.engrave: Engrave along the lines of the {target}
hints.vcarve: Carve inside the {target} with a V-bit, deeper where they are wider
hints.relief_rough: Clear the material above {model} in levels, a flat end mill being the usual choice
hints.relief_finish: Finish {model} with parallel passes, a ball end mill being the usual choice

Operations.missingDrill: Add a drill or an end mill to your tool library: V-bits can't drill
Operations.missingEngrave: Add a V-bit or an end mill to your tool library: drill bits can't engrave
Operations.missingVCarve: Add a V-bit to your tool library to V-carve
Operations.noTool: Add a tool to your tool library first
Operations.selectModel: Select a model in the viewport first
Operations.selectPaths: Select paths in the viewport first
Operations.selectHint: Click paths in the top view to select what to cut; Shift+click to add more.
Operations.addToolLibrary: Add a tool to your <link>tool library</link> to create operations.
Operations.selectInsideTitle: Also select the closed paths inside the selected ones, such as a pocket's islands
Operations.renameTitle: Double-click or press F2 to rename

sideHints.top: Cut on the top side, first
sideHints.bottom: Cut on the bottom side, once the stock is turned over

Operations.estimateNote: Approximate: acceleration and tool changes aren't counted.
Operations.estimateNoMachine: Approximate: rapids aren't counted until the project has a machine, nor are acceleration and tool changes.

Bit.saveFailed: The bit couldn't be saved. Check your connection and try again.
Bit.name: Name

Machine.name: Name
Machine.manualSpindleHint: Speed set by hand (e.g. a trim router dial); the G-code sets no spindle speed.
Machine.spinUpHint: The wait after starting the spindle, before the bit enters the stock.
Machine.customGcodeHint: A filled-in block replaces what the post-processor writes at that point, so include everything your machine needs there (e.g. G21 and G90 in the program start). Leave a block empty to keep the default. Text is copied as is, apart from placeholders.

startHints.preset: Pick your router; its documented settings are filled in for you.

NewMachine.noMatch: No preset matches “{query}”. Start from scratch to describe your machine yourself.
NewMachine.check: Check the values below against your build; you can change any of them, now or later.

Shell.chooseMachine: Choose a machine in the project properties first
Shell.addOperation: Add or enable an operation first
Shell.saveFailed: {message} Changes are no longer saved; export the project to keep them.
Shell.saveError: {message} Changes are saved again once this is fixed.
Shell.saveCopy: Save a copy of this bit
Shell.editCatalog: Catalog bits stay as they are. This saves your copy to your library and uses it in every operation of this project that uses the catalog bit.
Shell.editLibrary: Changes the bit in your library and in every operation of this project that uses it.
Shell.notUpdated: The bit was saved, but these operations keep the bit as it was:
Shell.newBitDescription: Adds a bit to your library and picks it for this operation.
Shell.simulateTitle: Play back the cut move by move
Shell.exportFailed: This project couldn't be exported. Check your connection and try again.
Shell.exportedFiles: The G-code is in one file per side, saved as {files}. If your browser asked whether to allow several downloads, allow it, or the bottom side's file is missing.
Shell.exportedWithWarnings: The G-code was exported with warnings:
Shell.leaveAnyway: {error} Leave it anyway? Changes not saved will be lost; export the project first to keep them.

BugReport.description: This opens a new GitHub issue with your report filled in. Nothing is sent until you submit it there, which needs a GitHub account.
BugReport.title: Title
BugReport.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Pocket leaves an island uncut
BugReport.what: What happened, and what did you expect?
BugReport.noFiles: GitHub can't receive files from the app. After opening the issue, paste or drop them into it.
BugReport.copyFailed: The screenshot couldn't be copied: save it instead.
BugReport.project: The project, if it helps: export it from the operations pane and drop the file in.
BugReport.opened: The issue opened in your browser. Add what you want from above, then submit it there.
BugReport.copiedReport: The report was too long for the link, so it was copied: paste it into the GitHub issue that opened.
BugReport.notCopied: The report is too long for the link and couldn't be copied. Shorten it and try again.

Versions.unsaved: The project has changes that couldn't be saved. Save them first.
Versions.editing: Finish the change you're making first.
Versions.restoreConfirm: Restore “{name}”? It replaces the project's contents, which are kept as a version first. Undo history is cleared.
Versions.renamePrompt: Rename version (leave blank to show its date)
Versions.deleteConfirm: Delete the version “{name}”? This can't be undone.
Versions.empty: No versions yet. Save one to go back to this state later.

Stock.guestMachine: G-code is made for your machine, which is saved in a free account or the desktop app. <button>Set up your machine</button>.
Stock.noMachine: No machine set. Choose the machine this project is for to export G-code.
Stock.pickHint: Click a point in the viewport; it snaps to stock anchors, vertices, centres and bounding boxes nearby. Esc or right-click cancels.
Stock.touchOffHint: A spot of the stock top no operation cuts, so Z can be zeroed on it after a tool change.
Stock.twoSidedHint: Cut the stock from the top, turn it over, and cut it from below.
Stock.partingDepthHint: Below the stock top, where the two sides meet around the models: each side cuts down to it there, and all of the model it can see.
Stock.twoSidedOff: {count, plural, one {# operation is} other {# operations are}} on the bottom side. Turning two-sided off moves {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} to the top side.
Stock.padTooWide: Must fit on the stock: at most {size}
Stock.padCentre: Its centre, from the stock's bottom-left corner. Resizing it keeps the centre where it is.
Stock.padOff: Part of the pad is off the stock, so there may be nothing to zero Z on there.
Stock.pinsHint: Pins on the flip axis line the turned-over stock up with the top side.
Stock.pinPositionHint: Each pin's distance along the flip axis from the stock's centre.
Stock.pinOff: A pin is off the stock.
Stock.noPinBit: Add a drill bit of the pins' size, or a smaller end mill, to drill them.
Stock.edgesHint: Push this corner of the stock into a fence corner for both sides. The sides only meet if the stock is exactly {size} along {axis}: measure it.
Stock.idlePinDrills: {count, plural, one {# drill of the pins cuts} other {# drills of the pins cut}} nothing without pins.
Stock.holdingTabsHint: Strips of stock the bottom side leaves at the parting depth, so the part stays held until the last pass. Drag them along the models' outlines in the top view.
Stock.holdingTabTooThick: Must be thinner than the bottom side's depth: less than {size}
Stock.holdingTabCount: {count, plural, =0 {No tabs} one {# tab} other {# tabs}}

Model.triangles: {count, plural, one {# triangle} other {# triangles}}. Cut from the top only: undercuts and overhangs are filled in, as the viewport shows.
Model.tooDeep: The model reaches deeper than the stock is thick: it is cut no deeper than the stock's bottom.
Model.borderNote: Left on every side by the next Fit to stock; editing it doesn't move the model.
Model.borderCapped: Left on every side by the next Fit to stock; editing it doesn't move the model. On this stock it leaves {size}, a quarter of its smaller side.
Model.originalTitle: Scale the model back to its size in the file
Model.fitTitle: Scale the model to fit inside the stock, leaving the border on every side
Model.positionHint: Where the model's {anchor, select, top_left {top left} top_center {top centre} top_right {top right} middle_left {middle left} middle_right {middle right} bottom_left {bottom left} bottom_center {bottom centre} bottom_right {bottom right} other {centre}} point is, measured from the zero. Moving it doesn't change the border that Fit to stock leaves.
Model.removeTitle: Also removes the {count, plural, one {operation} other {# operations}} that machine it

Drawing.borderNote: The space Fit to stock leaves on every side.
Drawing.borderCapped: The space Fit to stock leaves on every side. On this stock it leaves {size}, a quarter of its smaller side.
Drawing.fitTitle: Scale the drawing to fit inside the stock, leaving the border on every side
Drawing.positionHint: Where the drawing's {anchor, select, top_left {top left} top_center {top centre} top_right {top right} middle_left {middle left} middle_right {middle right} bottom_left {bottom left} bottom_center {bottom centre} bottom_right {bottom right} other {centre}} point is, measured from the zero. Drag the drawing in the top view to move it too.
Drawing.offStock: Part of the drawing lies outside the stock.
Drawing.removeTitle: Also removes the {count, plural, one {operation} other {# operations}} that only machine it
Drawing.duplicateTitle: Copies the drawing to its right, machined by the same operations

Text.heading: Text
Text.heightNote: Height measures the capital letters. Changing the text keeps it in place.
Text.tabsRemoved: Removed {count, plural, one {# tab} other {# tabs}} that no longer lay on the letters.
Text.convertTitle: Keep the letters as a drawing, machined by the same operations; it can no longer be edited as text

Import.start: Import an SVG or DXF drawing, or an STL model, to start.
Import.dpiQuestion: <name>{file}</name> gives its size in pixels, or not at all. How many pixels make an inch? Check the export settings of the program that made it.
Import.unitsQuestion: <name>{file}</name> doesn't say what unit its coordinates are in. Check the export settings of the program that made it.

viewHints.orbit: Drag to orbit, right-drag to pan, scroll to zoom

Viewport.simulateTitle: Simulate cutting: show the stock as it will look after the toolpaths
Viewport.nothing: Nothing to simulate: add or enable an operation in the workspace.
Viewport.previousTitle: Back to the start of the operation

sideHints.top: Show the top side, cut first
sideHints.bottom: Show the bottom side, seen from below once the stock is turned over

Viewport.bottomSideHint: Bottom side, seen from below. Pick the zero, select paths and edit tabs on the top side.
Viewport.topSideSimulationHint: Top side only: the stock before it is turned over, without the bottom side's cuts.

bits.title: Your bits
bits.body: Add the router bits you own, with their sizes and feeds. Operations pick their bit from this library.

machines.title: Your machine
machines.body: Describe your router once, or start from a preset. Its work area, feeds and G-code dialect apply to every project made for it.

new-project.title: Start a project
new-project.body: Create a project here, or import a project file. You can choose its machine now or later, before exporting G-code.

import.title: Import a drawing
import.body: Start from an SVG or DXF file: its paths become the shapes you cut.

properties.title: Project properties
properties.body: Set the units, the machine and the stock: the size and thickness of the material, and where its zero is.

select.title: Select paths
select.body: Click a path in the viewport to select it, and Shift+click to add more. Operations cut what is selected.

operations.title: Add operations
operations.body: Add an operation (profile, pocket, drill, engrave or V-carve) for the selected paths, then pick its bit and depths.

preview.title: Preview the toolpaths
preview.body: The viewport shows the toolpaths of every enabled operation, with rapid moves told apart from cuts. Check them before you cut.

export-gcode.title: Export G-code
export-gcode.body: When the toolpaths look right, export the G-code and run it with your usual sender.

versions.title: Versions
versions.body: Optional: save a named version before a big change, and restore it whenever you need.

Placeholders.list: On export, {padX} becomes the touch-off pad's centre X, {padY} becomes the touch-off pad's centre Y and {safeZ} becomes the machine's safe Z, all measured from the zero.
